answer: A shared staking lagoon makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a deposit of real value before it can transact, and the deposit is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Like a mesa that stands only because its rock is solid, reputation builds slowly on that stake through verified work, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake identities — each one needs its own locked deposit and history, and cedar-slow growth means faking a trustworthy crowd costs more than the fraud could earn.
